newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures end down, specs sell on close.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures end down, specs sell on close.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures came under pressure by late-session speculative selling and settled just over the day's lows, market sources said.
The selling accelerated when the benchmark May contract fell below its downside target of 75.20 cents and triggered stops, pushing the spot month to its low of 74.85 cents.
May settled down 0.70 to 74.91 cents a lb, having ranged from 75.85 to 74.85 cents. The deferred months closed down 0.60 to 0.12 cent.
Volume was estimated at 4,500 lots compared to Friday's official 8,682 lots.
"The market needs to test the lower levels to get new sales registered," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes, said.
She noted that new-crop December managed to limit losses, reflecting fears that ongoing rain and potential flooding in the Mississippi Delta could slash planted cotton area in the 1997/98 season.
Players await Tuesday's spec/hedge report with expectations for the speculators to be shown holding a 5-10 percent net long position.
Rain in South America over the weekend was mildly supportive to prices, market sources said. Dry weather has returned to Australia during the harvest.

Argentina said today it exported 354,825 tonnes of cotton fiber in 1996, making it the fourth largest exporter in the world. The government did not release a comparative figure for the previous season.
